# Final Review Arbiter
**Producer:** agent:codex/gpt-5.4

## Summary

Rejected `fr-2-7a419098` because the reviewed worktree still has zero DIC shortcut defaults and the cited closed-system tests pass; accepted `fr-2-abc5b76f` because this patch adds alkalinity to the budget-helper assertion API but leaves some failure-message lines incorrectly hard-coded to `mg`.

## Rulings

- `fr-2-7a419098`: Reject
  The reviewed worktree does not contain the cited DIC-default change. In `.claude/worktrees/tanksim-6e5.4.7/crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs`, `ProcessParams::default()` still sets `respiration_dic_rate_mg_c_per_g_per_hour` and `photosynthesis_dic_rate_mg_c_per_g_per_hour` to `0.0`, and the patch diff does not touch the shared closed-system helpers in `budget_tracking.rs` or `budget_helpers.rs`. Targeted runs of `cargo test -p tank_core test_closed_system_c_conservation` and `cargo test -p tank_core closed_system_n_and_c_conserved_via_helpers` both pass in the reviewed worktree, so this amendment is describing a failure mode from another tree/history, not a present defect in the code under review.
- `fr-2-abc5b76f`: Accept
  The patch under review does add `Element::Alkalinity` to the public budget-helper surface and threads it through `BudgetInspector::net_delta`, `BudgetTotals`, and `select_element`, so alkalinity is now a supported assertion target in this worktree. But `crates/tank_core/src/budget_helpers.rs` still hard-codes `mg` in the per-system line (`474`) and the per-tick assertion text (`496`, `502`), while the headline and before/after lines were already switched to `meq`. That means an alkalinity failure would emit mixed, incorrect units. The planner rejection relies on older code without `Element::Alkalinity`, which is not the code currently being reviewed.
